narrative: Markets are navigating a volatile period characterized by a rotation away from concentrated AI-tech leadership toward defensive and retail sectors. While systematic flows and resilient consumer spending have provided support, investors are increasingly wary of regulatory scrutiny surrounding Nvidia and the potential economic drag from proposed broad-based Section 301 tariffs. Inflation remains a persistent concern, with core PCE accelerating to 3.3%, complicating the Federal Reserve's path forward. Consequently, the market is balancing AI-driven growth optimism against rising geopolitical friction and questions regarding the sustainability of corporate margins. Overall sentiment remains mixed as participants digest these competing macro and micro-level pressures.

Nasdaq.why: The index faces high volatility as investors rotate out of AI hardware leaders amid governance concerns and regulatory scrutiny, despite occasional surges driven by specific company news.

S&P 500.why: The index shows resilience by finding support near the 7,000 level, with weakness in mega-cap tech being partially offset by gains in defensive and retail sectors.

Gold.why: Gold was not covered in the provided notes.

Oil.why: Brent crude has seen upward pressure due to shifting sentiment, though easing prices have also been noted as a factor helping to alleviate inflation concerns.

priced_in: Two to three additional Fed rate hikes in the near term
Peak AI capital expenditure for the coming year
Potential deceleration in tech earnings growth relative to valuations
G-shaped economy with resilient consumer spending
Increased market uncertainty due to potential trade friction and tariffs
debates: The sustainability of AI-driven earnings growth versus valuation concerns
